title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous pages Grothendieck attaches to a simplicial set X_* and a base ring k a bigraded divided-power ('pd') de Rham complex C^{..}_DRpd(X_*,k). It is a module over the divided-power polynomial algebra k{T}. Its quotient by (T-1) recovers Sullivan's polynomial de Rham complex rationally, and it carries a cup product refining RΓ(X_*,k). In remark b) he says the pd structure on the augmentation ideal is important. He asks whether, for simply connected X_* with finiteness conditions, C^{..}_DRpd(X_*,k) with all its structure determines the homotopy type.

This page makes that question precise in three steps.
(1) Axiomatize 'virtual' pd de Rham complexes over k. These are bigraded, augmented, associative, anticommutative (alternating) differential k-algebras concentrated in bidegrees >= 0. The differential has bidegree (-1,+1); he had first offered (0,+1) 'au choix' and crossed it out. They carry divided powers on the augmentation ideal, compatible with d in the sense d(x^{[n]}) = x^{[n-1]} dx. He imposes a condition on the shifted cohomology objects H^{.q}(C^{..})[-q], whose exact wording is uncertain. Under it one recovers from C^{..} an object of D(k) with an associative, anticommutative multiplicative structure, i.e. the analogue of RΓ(X,k) with its cup product.
(2) Form a 'derived category' (DRpd) of such objects by inverting quasi-isomorphisms. Then X_* ↦ C^{..}_DRpd(X_*,k) gives a functor (Hot) → (DRpd) from homotopy types.
(3) Conjecture/question for k = Z. Restricted to connected, simply connected homotopy types with finitely generated H_i(X,Z), does this functor induce an equivalence onto pd de Rham complexes over Z with H^0 ≅ Z, H^1 = 0 and all H^i finitely generated over Z?

This is an integral analogue of Sullivan's (and Quillen's) rational equivalence between simply connected finite-type rational homotopy types and minimal cdga's. The divided powers are meant to supply the extra structure needed over Z. The next page records partial negative results on recovering Steenrod/Whitney operations, and the need to first define Sullivan-type minimal models (never done).
errors: Divided powers on an anticommutative graded algebra are normally imposed only on even-degree elements, since odd x have x^2 = 0. The page does not specify the parity convention.

The proposed equivalence is very likely false as stated. Strictly associative and graded-commutative algebra structures over Z (even with divided powers) tend to kill or mishandle Steenrod operations. Later work (Mandell 2006) shows that integrally even E∞ cochains are only faithful, not full, on finite-type nilpotent spaces. Grothendieck's own remark c) on the next page reports negative results on recovering cohomology operations from the multiplicative pd structure. Whether the extra T/bigrading data rescues the statement is left completely open.
The condition on H^{.q}(C^{..})[-q] is illegible/ambiguous ('p.d.-nombres [?]'). The exact axiom ensuring a well-defined object of D(k) is not recoverable with confidence.

ideas.what: Abstract category of bigraded pd-augmented anticommutative dg algebras ('virtual pd de Rham complexes') with differential of bidegree (-1,+1) and compatibility d(x^{[n]}) = x^{[n-1]}dx, localized at quasi-isomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: homotopy theory of divided-power (pd) cdga's / integral Sullivan-type algebraic models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Divided power dg algebras: Cartan, Berthelot (crystalline). Integral polynomial/pd forms on simplices: Cenkl–Porter (1980s), Ekedahl (2002)
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts. Related themes ('schématisation', algebraic models of homotopy types) appear in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and letters to Breen/Quillen; unsure for this specific pd formulation.

ideas.what: Functor (Hot) → (DRpd) sending a homotopy type to its pd de Rham complex, and the question whether it is an equivalence on simply connected types with f.g. integral homology onto complexes with H^0=Z, H^1=0, H^i f.g.
ideas.modern_name: integral homotopy theory via cochain algebras (integral Sullivan theorem / schematization over Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mandell (E∞ cochains, p-adic 2001, integral 2006); Toën (affine stacks, schematization over Z); Horel (cosimplicial binomial rings, ~2022); Ekedahl (integral minimal models, 2002)
ideas.where_published: Schematization problem in Pursuing Stacks (1983) is related, but this explicit pd-de Rham formulation with these hypotheses seems unpublished

missed.claim: An explicit 1975-76 conjecture: integral pd de Rham complexes of simplicial sets (bigraded over k{T}, recovering Sullivan forms mod T-1) give an equivalence between simply connected finite-type integral homotopy types and a derived category of pd-dga's with H^0=Z, H^1=0, H^i f.g. It predates Ekedahl, Mandell, Toën and Horel and uses the same finiteness hypotheses later found to be the right ones.
missed.quote: on peut se demander si ça [se] restreint aux types connexes et simplement connexes avec des H_i(X,Z) de t.f. (cas k=Z) induit une équivalence avec les "complexes de DRpd sur Z tels que H^0(C^{..}) ≃ k, H^1(C^{..}) = 0, les H^i(C^{..}) de t.f. sur Z !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck formulated the integral-models program in a specifically pd/crystalline-flavoured form before Pursuing Stacks. The bigraded k{T}-structure (a pd 'Rees parameter' interpolating to Sullivan forms at T=1) is a construction not obviously present in the later literature. It is worth comparing to Cenkl–Porter pd forms, Ekedahl's integral minimal models and Horel's binomial models, to see whether the T-structure carries information (e.g. on Steenrod operations) that strict pd-cdga's lack.

missed.claim: Implicit link between crystalline/pd technology (divided powers compatible with d, as in the de Rham–Witt / crystalline world) and integral homotopy theory of spaces. The later literature mostly reached integral models via E∞ or binomial structures rather than pd de Rham complexes.
missed.quote: avec p.d. sur l'idéal d'augmentation, compatibles avec la diff (d(x^{(n)}) = x^{(n-1)}dx)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Recent work relating derived de Rham/crystalline cohomology, derived pd-rings and homotopy types (e.g. via derived commutative rings and Toën's affine stacks) could test whether a pd model with the T-grading is closer to fully faithful than strict cdga's.

deep.surprise_reason: A precise, early (1975-76) unpublished conjecture of an integral Sullivan-type equivalence using divided-power de Rham complexes, with exactly the later-standard finiteness hypotheses. The general aspiration is known from Pursuing Stacks and the 1976 IHES talk. The conjecture is probably false as stated, and the program was later pursued independently by others, so the surprise is moderate.
